messages.subject: poly () - which type of orth. polynomials is used?
messages.subject_clean: poly () - which type of orth. polynomials is used?
messages.body_plain:
Hello there,

I have been trying to find out which type of orthogonal polynomial the
poly() function is based on, but I didn't find it in the help pages or
anywhere else.
Does anyone know whether they are Legendre polynomials, or a different type?

(I want to reconstruct curves on the basis of the calculated coefficients.)

Thanks!

Best
Laura

On Thu, Feb 14, 2008 at 08:44:55PM +0100, Laura Herbst wrote:
> I have been trying to find out which type of orthogonal polynomial the
> poly() function is based on, but I didn't find it in the help pages or
> anywhere else.
> Does anyone know whether they are Legendre polynomials, or a different type?
>
> (I want to reconstruct curves on the basis of the calculated coefficients.)

I don't know anything about poly(), but in most cases where I've
needed to draw fitted curves (e.g., when doing spline fitting), it
turned out that there was a version of the predict() method defined
for my object, and that was what I needed.  I see that there is some
sort of predict() defined on poly objects; does it help?

-- Nathaniel

-- 
Electrons find their paths in subtle ways.

messages.subject: any update on vowel space ellipses or IPA...?
messages.subject_clean: any update on vowel space ellipses or IPA...?
messages.body_plain:
I just got a question about the vowel space ellipse code I posted way back in 
June 2007, asking if I have that "finalized version" I seemed to promise:

http://www.mail-archive.com/r-lang-J8UlxMCpGvdVdeU8dOWy+g at public.gmane.org/msg00033.html

In fact I don't, partly since I wrote it for fun and don't use it in my own 
research and then ... life moved on ... and partly since the very next day 
Katalin Mady posted about Emu-related code for doing the same thing:

http://www.mail-archive.com/r-lang-J8UlxMCpGvdVdeU8dOWy+g at public.gmane.org/msg00034.html

But given the query, I wonder if any of the real-live phoneticians on this list 
would be interested in either finalizing my code, or hacking the emu package to 
make a stand-alone function of the sort I sketched out.

--
